chunks: Have you not considered those who went out of their homes in thousands, fearing death, so Allah said to them, 'Die,' then He restored them to life? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
ai.seo_question: Who are the people who went out of their homes in thousands fearing death mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah?
ai.summary: While traditionally linked to the Banu Qaynuqa, Shia exegetes like Al--Ayyashi also associate this verse with the Banu Nadir or the general phenomenon of divine resurrection, emphasizing Allah's absolute power over life and death. The phrase 'die then live' underscores the concept of *Mawt* (death) as a transition rather than an end, serving as a sign for those who reflect. This highlights the contrast between Allah's abundant grace (*Fadl*) and the ingratitude (*Kufr*) of the majority, a recurring theme in Surah Al-Baqarah.
